notes.title: Devlog: The Inspiration Behind the Project of Feastopia
notes.content:
[h3]Hail, Contractors of the Culinary Capital![/h3][p][/p][h3]This is our very first development log, and we hope it gives you a deeper look into the journey behind the game. Our story begins with the initial spark of inspiration for [b]Feastopia[/b].[/h3][p][/p][p align="start"]Now, let Reinhart take it from here![/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][p]Hello everyone, I’m Reinhart from WhiteStar Studio, producer of [i]Thriving City: Song[/i] and [i]Feastopia[/i].[/p][p][/p][p align="start"]The conception of [i]Feastopia[/i] came at a rather delicate time—right after the full release of [i]Thriving City: Song[/i]. Around then, the whole studio was in a state of burnout. For our programmers and artists, it was the fatigue that came with over four years of continuous development on one project. But for me, it was more about hitting a creative block—I wasn’t sure how to move forward with game design.[/p][p][/p][p align="start"]I’d come into the studio every day, open the [i]Thriving City[/i] project files, and just feel lost. Even with all the feedback and suggestions from players, I had no idea where to even begin. It’s a tough spot for a game designer—even if you pause a project, what do you do next?[/p][p][/p][p align="start"]Right in the middle of all that mental wrestling, my little one at home—who’s always clamoring for milk—suddenly inspired me: [i]What if we blended nurturing elements into a city-builder to make urban planning more engaging?[/i][/p][p][/p][p][img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//45214286/38ff62805662ff9391a3f670f8ba8e83218d038d.jpg"][/img]（Yep! That’s my kiddo! ）[/p][p][/p][p]Once this new direction popped into my head, I couldn’t wait to bounce the idea off the rest of the team. Everyone loved it, and we started brainstorming more details together: a city forever locked in spring-like warmth, where weather shifts would affect operations rather than ruin the vibe; a food-based nurturing system allowing for tons of delicious dishes; architecture that looked good enough to eat—like something out of a candy-coated dream. In fact, once we aligned on [i]Feastopia[/i]’s world, the name itself just clicked. It instantly felt like the perfect expression of the game’s heart.[/p][p][/p][p align="start"]But blending nurturing mechanics organically into city-building posed some real design challenges. And let’s be real—we couldn’t just have players raising an actual baby, right? So we expanded the lore. During brainstorming, we looked to [i]Against the Storm[/i] for roguelite inspiration, and eventually shifted the “creature to nurture” toward our studio’s two chonky cats.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//45214286/444dc57e4b8766e0b5b3185e50247d0311d74bed.jpg"][/img]（Our studio mascots—always cuddling! ）[/p][p][/p][p]Around that time, our art team was experimenting with new styles. They soon realized that using realistic cats as the city’s central “creature” lacked fantasy appeal and limited architectural creativity. Since the new game revolved heavily around food, we took inspiration from mythical beasts like the Taotie and Behemoth—and that’s how we eventually arrived at [b]Dango[/b]: a round, squishy, utterly adorable being![/p][p][/p][p][img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//45214286/da3edc908e0778f6b5ccb3395c2604b8537d3b97.png"][/img][/p][p]（Early concept art of Dango! ）[/p][p][/p][p]Watching my own child grow day by day also got me thinking about giving Dango distinct life stages. In [i]Feastopia[/i], Dango is very much like a child—behaving differently in its baby phase, and developing unique traits based on what you feed it. These traits then translate into different buffs affecting your city, forming part of the roguelite mechanics.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//45214286/44ce41c9347607ee66e9aecff99dd2a9d07933aa.png"][/img]
[/p][p]The more we developed [i]Feastopia[/i]’s gameplay, the more hooked we became—and slowly, I found my rhythm again. Now, the whole team is pouring heart and soul into this new project. We’re in the final stages of development, constantly polishing the demo, and working hard to deliver a fresh, fun, and fascinating city-building experience![/p][p][/p][p][img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//45214286/0977861ff5894589ebabea69cfcf182be1561e69.png"][/img][/p][p]If you have any[i] [/i]feedback – share bugs, ideas, or culinary fantasies, welcome to join our community in the[i] [/i][url="https://discord.gg/XmxVwhypnt"]Feastopia Discord[/url][i]![/i][/p]

notes.title: Version 0.1.3.4 Demo Update Note
notes.content: [p]Welcome to Feastopia! Lately we've deployed the following updates to the demo:[/p][p][/p][olist][*][p]Fixed a flickering issue with the pause button for resource supply in the [b]Market[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed display issues with resource count statistics.[/p][/*][*][p]Adjusted values for residents' food consumption.[/p][/*][*][p]Improved visual feedback for natural resources when placing [b]Gathering Huts[/b] and [b]Mines[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Added detailed tooltips to the [b]Total Population[/b] display.[/p][/*][*][p]Reworked delivery logic and rewards for [b]Population Reward Quests[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Adjusted completion logic and rewards for [b]Exploration Events[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Reduced the resource cost to clear [b]Fog of War[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed incorrect text descriptions after completing certain quests.[/p][/*][*][p]Corrected erroneous reward values for [b]Exploration Events[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Adjusted rewards for the [b]Wishlist[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Optimized English translations and display effects across multiple UI elements.[/p][/*][*][p]Improved descriptions for various effect and button tooltips.[/p][/*][*][p]Tweaked effects and related values in the[b] Land of Wish[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Adjusted the [b]Atmosphere Gauge[/b] impact of various buildings.[/p][/*][*][p]Changed the starting quantities of the 3 [b]Selectable Resources[/b] in the beginner setup.[/p][/*][*][p]Slightly tweaked the distribution weighting of natural resource nodes.[/p][/*][*][p]Reworked the base scoring of all resources; all resources now contribute to a category score.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Gathering Huts[/b], [b]Mines[/b], [b]Orchard Groves[/b], and the [b]Merchant Guildhall[/b] are now available as starting buildings.[/p][/*][*][p]Adjusted the consumption rate of resources required to maintain population. Upgrading dwellings will now slightly increase the consumption rate of lower-tier resources.[/p][/*][*][p]Adjusted the quality tiers of certain foods.[/p][/*][*][p]Temporarily removed [b]Gold Bar[/b], [b]Paint[/b], [b]Rubber[/b], [b]Sheep Intestines[/b], [b]Alcohol[/b], [b]Poison Potion[/b], [b]Stationery[/b], and [b]Lavender[/b] from the game. Related production recipes, items, and facility functions have been redesigned.[/p][/*][*][p]Adjusted the acquisition logic for [b]Blueprints[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Adjusted the acquisition logic for [b]Recipes[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Adjusted the distribution weighting of [b]Exploration Events[/b].[/p][/*][/olist][p][/p][h3][b]PS: Due to the significant changes in this update, save data from previous versions is no longer compatible. Please start a new game.[/b][/h3][h3][/h3][p][/p][p][b]Join our community![/b][/p][p][i]We crave your feedback – share bugs, ideas, or culinary fantasies in the [/i][url="https://discord.gg/XmxVwhypnt"]Feastopia Discord[/url][i]![/i][/p]

notes.title: Feastopia: Free Playable Demo Now Available!

notes.title: Patch 0.0.6 update log.
notes.content: [p]Huge thanks to everyone who jumped into the Feastopia playtest! Your feedback means the world to us, and we’re hard at work making the game even more awesome based on what you’ve shared. During this playtest, we’ve been squashing bugs and tackling the most urgent stuff. Here’s what we’ve polished up and fixed in the latest update:[/p][list][*][p]Tweaked how icons look for attached buildings[/p][/*][*][p]Made the fire station a starting building by default[/p][/*][*][p]Boosted the odds of getting blueprints for buildings tied to common materials for construction[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a glitch where the livestock ranch blueprint wasn’t displaying right[/p][/*][*][p]Added clearer explanations for atmosphere debuff rules[/p][/*][*][p]Sorted out some icon text mix-ups[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed bugs with certain wishlist tasks showing incorrectly[/p][/*][*][p]Added helpful prompts when you’re about to build something[/p][/*][*][p]Resized attached buildings for the fisheries cabin[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Fixed an issue where upgrading houses would spit back materials[/p][/*][*][p]Cleared up mistakes in food labels[/p][/*][*][p]Stopped blueprints from popping up more than once[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed mismatched beverages, icons, and fonts in the gourmet house[/p][/*][*][p]Now you can hit Esc to cancel pre-building, and hit it again to close the build menu[/p][/*][*][p]Tweaked how some blueprints unlock[/p][/*][*][p]Bumped up the resources needed to clear fog just a bit[/p][/*][*][p]Added a cool glow to icons for all attached buildings[/p][/*][*][p]Made the gourmet recipe UI look slicker[/p][/*][*][p]Increased the odds of getting blueprints for buildings that produce construction materials[/p][/*][*][p]Increased the common materials for construction needed for some basic buildings[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Fixed a screen flash when opening the new level interface after the tutorial[/p][/*][*][p]Stopped the camera from going rogue when opening the wishlist while moving[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed the spacebar not pausing/resuming during road-building, demolish, repair, or move modes[/p][/*][*][p]Made sure the build menu updates resources in real-time so clicks work properly[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where the game would freeze and become unresponsive after Dango finished eating[/p][/*][*][p]Stopped Missions of the Cat God from resetting when you reload a save[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed data errors for Missions of the Cat God[/p][/*][*][p]Sorted out save file loading issues during lag[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed incorrect star rating color display on the top-right corner of food items[/p][/*][*][p]Cleaned up UI glitches after loading[/p][/*][*][p]Disabled blueprint refresh and “think again” button in the tutorial[/p][/*][*][p]Extended the max view distance[/p][/*][*][p]Added more wish fruits as a reward for clearing levels[/p][/*][*][p]Unified text for cucumbers and attached buildings across the game[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]All buildings that make materials for construction can now get blueprints at difficulty 1[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed icons not following attached buildings when you move them[/p][/*][*][p]Corrected info-display of Missions of the Cat God in the top-right corner[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed some cases where saves wouldn’t load[/p][/*][*][p]Stopped atmosphere debuff from bouncing around unexpectedly[/p][/*][*][p]Added Q/E keys for quick field-of-view changes[/p][/*][*][p]Set default volume (master, music, sound effects) to a comfy 50%[/p][/*][*][p]Game now auto-picks your system’s language[/p][/*][*][p]Beefed up the tutorial map to a 100x100 grid[/p][/*][*][p]Added smooth edge-of-screen mouse movement[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed the help bar getting cut off at certain resolutions[/p][/*][*][p]Added clear rules for picking starting buffs in the UI[/p][/*][*][p]Buildings go semi-transparent when you’re in demolish mode[/p][/*][*][p]Buildings that pause production now give super clear “on hold” notices[/p][/*][/list][p]Thanks again for your support![/p]
